name: Climate Resilience and Sustainability
summary: How agri-energy investments contribute to climate adaptation and mitigation in Uganda's agricultural sector, building farmer resilience and reducing emissions.
description: Climate change is profoundly affecting Uganda's agriculture through erratic rainfall, prolonged droughts, flooding, shifting seasons, and increased pest and disease pressure. Agri-energy plays a dual role in climate resilience: first as an adaptation measure by enabling irrigation, improved food storage, and reduced climate risk; and second as a mitigation measure by replacing fossil fuels and reducing deforestation from firewood collection. This thematic area explores both dimensions, documenting how agri-energy interventions build farmer resilience to climate shocks, preserve ecosystems, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and support Uganda's climate commitments under the Paris Agreement and the NDC framework.
whyItMatters: Agriculture in Uganda is predominantly rainfed and therefore highly vulnerable to climate variability. Agri-energy investments that enable irrigation, improved storage, and clean energy supply are also investments in climate adaptation. Without incorporating climate resilience into agri-energy programming, gains from technology adoption can quickly be reversed by climate shocks.
